brief: Zero Hedge's weekly recap argues the AI trade's financing problem, not inflation, drove markets. CoreWeave's bonds and CDS blew out (CDS implying roughly 63% default odds), neocloud equities fell 20% in five sessions, and hedge funds reversed all their AI buying since January 2025, pulling NDX down almost 6% and the Kospi down 20% on the week. The bond market read this AI credit stress as a growth shock: despite September CPI (3.7% y/y) and PPI (6.3% y/y) both running hot and October hike odds spiking to 55%, the 10Y fell to a three-week low near 5.08% as AI debt issuance stopped crowding out Treasury demand. Fed Chair Warsh then declined to pre-commit, saying conditions had "broadly conformed" to expectations, which Goldman reads as an October pause with one more hike in December; hike odds fell to 13%. Oil also rose on Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Hormuz tanker sinkings, but bonds ignored it. Goldman's Privorotsky thinks the selloff overreacted; the author expects credit to keep dragging equities lower.
